short: Finite maximiser unique up to flip

statements.markdown:
At a fixed finite size the picture is different. If $\sigma,\tau$
differ at $k$ sites, precisely the $k(n-k)$ edges crossing that set change
their spin product. Their independent Gaussian contributions give
$$
\operatorname{Var}(H_n(\sigma)-H_n(\tau))=\frac{4k(n-k)}n.
$$
For $0<k<n$ this is positive, so the two energies tie with probability
zero. A finite union over pairs, together with
$H_n(-\sigma)=H_n(\sigma)$, shows that almost surely the exact maximum
has one maximizing pair $\{\sigma_*,-\sigma_*\}$.
statements.section: 9.3 Near-ground configurations at a prescribed overlap

statements.markdown:
At a fixed finite size, almost surely the only exact maximisers are
a configuration and its global reversal. Indeed, two configurations
that are neither equal nor global reversals differ in some pair product.
Their energy difference is then a Gaussian with positive variance, so a
tie has probability zero, and there are only finitely many pairs.

Reversing all the signs of one configuration
preserves its energy and reverses the sign of its overlap with another.
